system.summary: Unspaced 1- and 2-digit homophonic substitution with interleaved single- and two-digit nulls (59 codes recovered from ciphertext: 49 letter codes and 10 nulls); distinct from the Ceva key of targets/francia346.
system.sibling_key: Distinct from the Ceva key (targets/ceva1632, targets/francia346); mismatch tested by scripts/test_ceva_mismatch.py using R5635 as positive control.

prior_solution.where: Contemporary 1633 decipherment leaves exist in Francia 346 on R5634, R5638, and R5639. No modern published key or reading of this alternate cipher is known (distinct from Lasry's published Ceva key). None of the clerk's leaves was opened, copied, or used.

conditions.human_role: Prabal Gupta ran the transcription, ciphertext-only key recovery, mechanical decode, strict sentence-level readings, and Ceva mismatch tests with AI assistance; clerk's leaves were not opened.
models: language models, not named at the contributor's request

solution.what: Machine transcription of the six DECODE cipher pages (R5634 ff. 190r-190v, R5638 ff. 218r-218v, R5639 ff. 220r-220v); 86 rows, 6,420 digits, 127 unread spans. Not verified by a person.

Recovered 59-code homophonic digit key (49 letter codes, 10 nulls) from ciphertext alone without opening the contemporary decipherments; frozen in branicki-1757 commit 681ed424 (2026-11-22 21:34:50 UTC-5, FROZEN.sha256).

scripts/test_ceva_mismatch.py compared key.tsv against the published Ceva key (targets/francia346) on R5635 (positive control) and R5634, R5638, R5639 against 100 digit-shuffled ciphertext controls using lang/lexicons/it.json.gz. Double dissociation: R5635 Ceva 23.1% >=5-letter word coverage (Z=+4.4) vs. alt 0.0% (Z=+0.3); R5638 alt 45.3% (Z=+28.0) vs. Ceva 4.1%; R5639 alt 42.5% (Z=+28.2) vs. Ceva 8.2%.

Added strictly aligned word-divided Italian readings (r5638_reading.md, r5639_reading.md) and English translations (r5638_en.md, r5639_en.md), verified mechanically by scripts/verify_readings.py with zero unmarked departures from the unedited decode: R5638 159/246 sure cipher words (0.646), R5639 115/202 sure cipher words (0.569). R5634 stays decoded, not read.

outcome.method_basis: 59-code unspaced 1- and 2-digit key recovered from ciphertext alone and applied mechanically via scripts/decode.py; R5638 and R5639 read in part as coherent Italian sentences without opening the contemporary clerk leaves.
outcome.fraction_read_source: scripts/verify_readings.py on r5638_reading.md and r5639_reading.md: 274 of 448 cipher words sure (R5638 159/246 = 0.646, R5639 115/202 = 0.569); R5634 remains decoded, not read.

texts.label: R5634, ff. 190r-190v
texts.summary: Short, broken letter (54 unread gaps) touching on compensation for pensions, letting a pension suffer, and a particular obligation. (Working guess from the decode; not a reading.)
texts.note: 23 rows, 1,211 digits, 557 letters, 122 nulls, 54 gaps. Decoded, not read; cipher words not counted.

texts.label: R5638, ff. 218r-218v

reading_review.by: contributor's AI model (not independent; awaiting maintainer review)
reading_review.note: Coherent 17th-century Italian diplomatic sentences on the enclosed letter, divided cipher sheet, priory renunciation, and 4,000-scudi provision (159 of 246 cipher words sure = 0.646, 87 holes); scripts/verify_readings.py confirms zero unmarked departures from the unedited mechanical decode. Not checked by a person or an independent reader.

texts.summary: An enclosed letter and divided sheet of cipher sent to V.E.: the writer considers renouncing a priory to declare himself an independent servant and insists on taking 4,000 scudi as provision to reimburse himself rather than serve as a salaried dependent, writing in strict confidence.
texts.note: 33 rows, 2,874 digits, 1,361 letters, 153 nulls, 16 transcription gaps. Reading strictly aligned to the unedited mechanical decode by scripts/verify_readings.py (159/246 sure cipher words, 87 holes).

texts.label: R5639, ff. 220r-220v

reading_review.by: contributor's AI model (not independent; awaiting maintainer review)
reading_review.note: Coherent Italian diplomatic clauses on the companion priory and 4,000-scudi compensation settlement and reply on arrival (115 of 202 cipher words sure = 0.569, 87 holes); scripts/verify_readings.py confirms zero unmarked departures from the unedited mechanical decode. Opening rows on f. 220r remain heavily gapped. Not checked by a person or an independent reader.

texts.summary: Companion letter to R5638 on the same priory and compensation settlement: denying self-interest, combining a 4,000-scudi payment with the equivalent and remainder of the priory, and replying to news of the recipient's arrival.
texts.note: 30 rows, 2,335 digits, 1,103 letters, 134 nulls, 57 transcription gaps. Reading strictly aligned to the unedited mechanical decode by scripts/verify_readings.py (115/202 sure cipher words, 87 holes).

R5638 (159/246 = 0.646) and R5639 (115/202 = 0.569) carry strictly aligned Italian readings and English translations; R5634 stays decoded, not read. first_break is set to 'unpublished prior' because contemporary 1633 clerk leaves exist in the archive while no modern reading or key was previously published.
